intro.title: Build typed sessionStorage wrapper
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed wrapper around the browser's sessionStorage API using TypeScript. You'll learn how to create a custom class that provides type safety, ensuring only specific data types can be stored and retrieved. The core programming concept involves using TypeScript generics to define flexible yet strict types for your storage operations. You'll work with key technologies like TypeScript classes, interfaces, and the native sessionStorage object. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe utility that prevents common errors and improves code reliability in web applications.
intro.usecase: Typed sessionStorage wrappers are commonly used in e-commerce checkout flows where user selections (shipping options, payment methods) need to persist across page navigation without server calls. In analytics dashboards, they maintain filter states (date ranges, metric selections) as users toggle between different report views. This pattern also appears in multi-step forms for applications or onboarding wizards, where partially completed data needs temporary storage with type safety to prevent data corruption during the user's session.
